The Story of Shivnandi Muni

I bow to Lord Jina, worshipped by the world, whose bright eye is omniscience, and I write the story of those who suffered bad results from studying scriptures at the improper time, so that the thoughtful may know that studying at the wrong time is not good and brings bad results.

Although Monk Shivnandi knew through his guru that the proper time for scriptural study is after the rising of the Shravan constellation, through the intense ripening of karma, he used to study scriptures at the improper time. The result was that, dying through false meditation, he was reborn as a massive fish in the Ganga River. Truly, through violating Lord Jina's command, this soul had to suffer the pains of a lower birth.

One day, a monk was studying scriptures on the riverbank. The fish heard his recitation. Through this, he remembered his past life. He then deeply regretted, saying, "Alas! Despite studying, I remained a fool. Turning away from Jain dharma, I bound sinful karma. This is the result — I had to take the body of a fish."

In this way, through self-condemnation and confession of his sinful karma, he took right faith with devotion, which brings welfare to all beings. Afterward, through worshipping Lord Jina and the ripening of merit, he became a great god in heaven. Truly, humans who practise dharma go to heaven and enjoy happiness, while sinners who act contrary to dharma go to lower births and suffer. Knowing this, the wise should worship dharma according to the teachings of Lord Jinendra with devotion, for dharma bestows all happiness.

One who has attained right knowledge gains fame throughout the world, attains all manner of excellent wealth, finds peace, and becomes the very embodiment of purity. Therefore, worthy souls should strive to obtain the pure knowledge of Lord Jina, which is worshipped by gods and Vidyadharas.

This story teaches that even the study of scriptures, if done at the wrong time, can lead to negative consequences. Monk Shivnandi, despite his learning, violated the rule about proper study times and was reborn as a fish. But even in that state, hearing the scriptures reminded him of his past life, and through confession and right faith, he was able to attain a heavenly birth. The wise should follow all rules of their tradition carefully, for even seemingly minor violations can have serious consequences.
